title: DRY FRUIT *laddoos*
name: Dry fruit laddoos
intro: No added sugar, ghee or oil. Dates and figs bind and sweeten, and the nuts bring the crunch.
ingredients: 1 cup chopped Zunera Medjool or Kalmi dates, pitted
steps: Dry-roast the almonds in a pan, stirring every so often, until they brown lightly. Set them aside.
Roughly chop the dates and the figs, and measure out 1 cup of chopped dates.
Lightly crush the cardamom pods, discard the skins and coarsely crush the seeds.
Put the dates, figs, cashews, raisins, coconut, cardamom and roasted almonds into a grinder or food processor and grind to a coarse mixture.
Shape the mixture into small balls with your hands.
Serve straight away, or store in an airtight box: a few days at room temperature, or a couple of weeks in the fridge.
tip: Keep the dates and figs: their stickiness is what holds the laddoos together. If your figs are very dry, soak them in hot water for a couple of hours, then drain and pat them dry before chopping.
photoBrief: A plate of dry fruit laddoos, a few broken open to show dates, figs and nuts, on a brass thali with a Zunera pouch behind. Warm side light. Square 1:1.

title: RICE *kheer*
name: Rice kheer
intro: Basmati rice slow-cooked in milk until thick and creamy, with cardamom, saffron and a handful of nuts and raisins.
steps: Rinse the rice a few times until the water runs clear, then soak it in water for 15 to 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, bring the milk to a boil in a heavy, wide pan over low to medium-low heat, stirring now and then so it does not stick.
Spoon 1 tbsp of the hot milk into a small bowl, let it cool until warm, and add the saffron.
Drain the rice and stir it into the boiling milk. Simmer uncovered on low heat, stirring at intervals, until the rice is about half cooked.
Stir in the sugar and keep simmering until the rice is almost cooked.
Add the cardamom, almonds, cashews, pistachios and the saffron milk. Cook on low heat until the rice is completely soft and the kheer has thickened, scraping the milk solids from the sides back in.
Turn off the heat and stir in the raisins. Serve hot, warm or chilled.
tip: Kheer thickens further as it cools. Keep leftovers in the fridge and eat within 1 to 2 days, loosening with a splash of milk when you reheat. The original recipe uses golden raisins; black raisins work the same way.
photoBrief: A clay bowl of creamy rice kheer topped with sliced almonds, pistachios and black raisins, a few saffron strands, a brass spoon beside it. Warm light. Square 1:1.

title: KESAR BADAM *milk*
name: Kesar badam milk
intro: Soaked almonds ground with sugar, cardamom and saffron, then warmed through in milk. Good hot, warm or chilled.
ingredients: ⅓ cup hot water, for soaking
steps: Rinse the almonds, cover them with ⅓ cup just-boiled water, and leave covered for 30 to 40 minutes.
Drain and peel the almonds. The skins slip off when you press them.
Put the almonds in a blender with the sugar, cardamom seeds, saffron and ¼ to ⅓ cup of the milk. Grind until very fine and smooth.
Scrape the paste into a saucepan. Swirl ½ cup of the milk around the blender jar to pick up what is left and add it to the pan, then pour in the remaining milk (about 1½ cups).
Warm on low heat, stirring now and then so it does not catch. Turn off the heat once it is hot; it does not need a hard boil.
Serve hot or warm, or chill it first. Garnish with sliced almonds or a few saffron strands if you like.
tip: Grind the almonds as fine as you can: coarse bits can irritate the throat. Instead of hot water, you can soak the almonds in room-temperature water for 8 hours.
photoBrief: Two glasses of pale-golden saffron almond milk with saffron strands on top, a small bowl of almonds beside them. Warm light. Square 1:1.

title: SHEER *khurma*
name: Sheer khurma
intro: The Eid classic: fine vermicelli simmered in milk with dates, nuts and raisins sautéed in ghee. Sheer means milk, and khurma means dates.
ingredients: 2 tbsp Zunera seeded black raisins, seeds removed
½ cup Zunera Ajwa or Kalmi dates, pitted and chopped (about 100 g)
1 tbsp rose water or kewra water
steps: Dry-roast the vermicelli in a pan on low heat, stirring often, until golden. Set aside.
In the same pan, heat the ghee and add the pistachios, almonds, cashews, raisins, dates and chironji. Sauté on low heat for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring often.
Bring the milk to a boil in a heavy pan over medium-low to medium heat, stirring a few times. Lower the heat and simmer for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring often, until it thickens slightly.
Add the roasted vermicelli and the sugar. Simmer on low to medium-low heat for 8 to 10 minutes, until the vermicelli is soft and the milk has reduced.
Add the cardamom, saffron, and all of the ghee, nut and date mixture. Turn off the heat and stir well. Taste and add more sugar if needed.
Stir in the rose water. Serve hot, warm or cold.
tip: The dates and raisins add plenty of sweetness, so taste before adding more sugar. The original recipe uses golden raisins; with seeded black raisins, slit each one and pick out the seeds first. Sheer khurma thickens as it cools.
photoBrief: A bowl of sheer khurma with vermicelli, slivered nuts and chopped dates on top, rose petals scattered on a festive tablecloth. Warm light. Square 1:1.

title: DATE *rolls*
name: Date rolls (dry fruit barfi)
intro: A Diwali favourite with no added sugar. Dates, figs and four kinds of nuts, rolled into logs and sliced.
ingredients: 140 to 150 g Zunera Mabroom, Rabia or Mashrook dates, pitted (about ¾ cup)
30 g Zunera pistachios, shelled (about ¼ cup)
30 g walnuts (about ¼ cup): Zunera walnut kernels, or cracked Zunera in-shell walnuts
2 tsp rose water, or ¼ to ½ tsp green cardamom powder (optional)
steps: Pour ⅓ cup of just-boiled water over the figs and raisins, cover, and leave for 20 minutes. Drain. (If your figs are soft, you can skip this.)
Meanwhile, pulse the almonds, cashews, pistachios and walnuts in a grinder 3 or 4 times, until they are in small bits. Do not grind them to a powder. Tip them out.
In the same jar, grind the chopped dates, figs and raisins to a coarse paste.
Heat the coconut oil in a frying pan and toast the sesame seeds on low heat until they crackle. Stir in the coconut, then add the nuts and sauté for 3 to 4 minutes on low heat.
Add the date paste and stir lightly. Turn off the heat, add the rose water or cardamom, and mix very well.
When the mixture is warm rather than hot, divide it in two. Rub a little oil on your palms and roll each half into a log.
Let the logs cool at room temperature, then slice. They keep for about a week in a covered container in the fridge.
tip: Instead of rolling, you can press the mixture into a greased tray and cut it into squares once cool. The original recipe uses golden raisins; black raisins work the same way.
photoBrief: Neat round slices of date and nut rolls on a brass plate, showing chopped pistachios and almonds in the dark date mixture, a few whole dates beside them. Warm light. Square 1:1.

title: IMLI KHAJUR *chutney*
name: Imli khajur chutney
intro: The sweet and tangy tamarind-date chutney that goes on every plate of chaat, pakoras and samosas.
ingredients: ½ cup seedless tamarind, tightly packed
½ cup Zunera Khudri or Fard dates, pitted
½ cup jaggery powder or grated jaggery, to taste
¼ to ½ tsp red chilli powder
Black salt or regular salt, to taste
steps: Put the tamarind, dates and water in a pan. Cook uncovered on low to medium-low heat for 8 to 9 minutes, until the tamarind and dates soften.
Add the jaggery and stir until it dissolves and the mixture thickens a little.
Add the cumin, coriander, dry ginger, chilli powder and salt. Simmer for 1 to 2 minutes more, then let it cool.
Blend until smooth, adding a little water if needed. Add more water if you like a thinner, pouring chutney.
Strain if you like, then store in an airtight jar in the fridge.
tip: It keeps for about a month in the fridge, so it is worth making a full batch for chaat, pani puri, bhel and samosas.
photoBrief: A small bowl of glossy dark-brown tamarind date chutney with a spoon, beside a plate of samosas and a few whole dates. Warm light. Square 1:1.

title: WALNUT BUTTER STUFFED *dates*
name: Walnut butter stuffed dates
intro: Three ingredients and five minutes. Soft Medjool dates filled with walnut butter and finished with chopped walnuts.
ingredients: 2 tbsp Zunera walnut kernels, finely chopped
steps: Cut each date lengthwise with a small, sharp knife and pull out the seed.
Spoon about 1 tsp of walnut butter into each date.
Sprinkle about ¼ tsp of chopped walnuts over each one.
Serve straight away, or keep in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 5 days.
tip: Shop-bought walnut butter works well. Give it a good stir before you use it.
photoBrief: Stuffed Medjool dates on a marble board, walnut butter filling and chopped walnuts on top. Overhead, natural light. Square 1:1.

title: KAJU ANJEER *milkshake*
name: Kaju anjeer milkshake
intro: Dried figs and cashews, soaked until soft and blended with cold milk. Thick, creamy and naturally sweet.
ingredients: 1 to 2 tsp raw sugar, jaggery powder or sugar (optional)
steps: Rinse the cashews and figs, then soak them in hot water for 30 to 45 minutes. Check the figs: if they are not soft yet, soak them a little longer.
Drain and put the cashews and figs in a blender (chop the figs if they are large) with ½ cup of the chilled milk. Blend to a smooth purée, or leave a few bits of fig for texture.
Add the remaining 2 cups of milk and blend again. If your blender jar is small, stir the purée into the milk in a bowl instead.
Taste, and add a little sugar or jaggery only if it needs it.
Pour into glasses and serve straight away.
tip: This makes a fairly thick shake. Add more milk if you prefer it thinner.
photoBrief: Two tall glasses of thick, beige fig and cashew milkshake, halved dried figs and a few cashews scattered around. Bright natural light. Square 1:1.

title: DRY FRUITS *milkshake*
name: Dry fruits milkshake
intro: Nuts, raisins, figs and a handful of dates blended with cold milk. Sweet without sugar and filling enough for breakfast.
ingredients: ¼ cup Zunera seedless black raisins
7 to 8 Zunera dates, pitted and chopped: Sukkari Rutab, Mazafati, Sugai, Rabbi or Sukkari Mufatal
2½ cups chilled milk: dairy, soy or any plant milk
1 tbsp chopped almonds or pistachios, to garnish
steps: Soak the figs in hot water for 30 minutes, or in room-temperature water for 1 to 2 hours, until soft. Soak the dates too if they are firm or chewy.
Rinse the nuts, raisins and dates. If you like, soak the nuts and raisins in hot water for 30 minutes as well, and peel the almonds.
Roughly chop the softened figs and the dates.
Put the nuts, raisins, dates, figs and saffron in a blender with ½ cup of the milk and blend to a fine paste.
Add the remaining 2 cups of milk, and a little sugar only if it needs it. Blend again.
Pour into glasses, scatter over the chopped nuts, and serve straight away.
tip: Soft dates such as Sukkari Rutab and Mazafati blend straight in; firmer ones such as Rabbi and Sukkari Mufatal are best soaked first. Drink it the same day.
photoBrief: Two tall glasses of creamy beige dry fruits milkshake topped with chopped pistachios and almonds, small bowls of dates, figs and nuts around them. Bright natural light. Square 1:1.

title: SAUDI COFFEE WITH *dates*
name: Saudi coffee with dates
intro: Gahwa, the cardamom coffee offered to every guest in Saudi Arabia. It is served unsweetened, because the dates on the side bring the sweetness.
ingredients: 40 g lightly roasted Arabic coffee, ground
A plate of Zunera dates, to serve: Khalas, Sukkari Rutab, Sukkari Mufatal, Sugai, Amber, Mabroom or Ajwa
steps: Bring the water to a boil in a coffee pot.
Add the coffee and let it boil over medium heat without stirring, for about 15 minutes. Boiling it much longer makes it darker, thicker and more bitter.
Add the cardamom 2 to 3 minutes before you take the pot off the heat. If you are using saffron, add it 3 to 4 minutes before the end.
Strain the coffee into a serving pot or a flask.
Pour a little at a time into small cups, and serve with a plate of dates.
tip: Do not sweeten the coffee. Put out two or three date varieties side by side so guests can taste the difference.
photoBrief: A brass dallah pouring pale gahwa into a small finjan cup, a plate of three date varieties beside it. Warm light. Square 1:1.

title: KHUBANI KA *meetha*
name: Khubani ka meetha
intro: The Hyderabadi wedding dessert. Dried apricots soaked, then cooked down to a thick, tangy-sweet compote.
ingredients: 2 to 3 tsp sugar, or to taste (optional)
steps: Rinse the apricots well. Soak them overnight in 2 to 2½ cups of water, or for 4 to 5 hours in warm water.
Lift the apricots out and keep the soaking water.
If your apricots have stones, press them out with your fingers. Mash or chop the apricots.

Put the apricots in a pan with 1 cup of the strained soaking water. Cook on low heat for 22 to 25 minutes, stirring now and then and mashing them with a spoon. Add a little more soaking water if it looks dry.
Add sugar to taste and cook for 5 to 6 minutes more.
Stir in the almonds and serve hot, warm or cold, on its own or with cream, custard or ice cream.
tip: Traditionally the kernels from inside the apricot stones go in at the end. Almonds are a good stand-in and taste much the same.
photoBrief: A glass bowl of glossy amber apricot compote topped with sliced almonds and a spoon of cream, dried apricots beside it. Warm light. Square 1:1.

title: MA'AMOUL *cookies*
name: Ma'amoul (date-filled cookies)
intro: The semolina shortbread cookies baked across the Middle East for Eid and Ramadan, each one wrapped around a spiced date filling.
ingredients: ½ cup butter or ghee, at room temperature
225 g date paste, made from about 20 pitted Zunera Khalas, Amber or Sufri dates (see the date paste recipe)
steps: Mix the semolina, flour, sugar and baking powder in a large bowl. Rub in the butter or ghee with your hands until evenly combined.
Add the milk in two batches, mixing after each, until you have a soft dough that rolls into balls.
Preheat the oven to 175°C and line two baking trays with baking paper.
For the filling, mix the date paste with the oil, cinnamon and cardamom. Oil your hands and roll it into 35 small balls, a little smaller than your mould.
Roll the dough into 35 balls, slightly larger than the filling balls.
Flatten a dough ball, set a date ball in the middle, and gently bring the dough up around it to seal. Roll it smooth between your palms.
Press it lightly into the mould, then tap the mould on a board to release it. Place it pattern side up on the tray. Repeat, leaving about 2.5 cm between cookies.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes, until the bottoms are lightly golden. Dust with icing sugar if you like.
tip: To make the filling from scratch, pit the dates, soak them in hot water for 15 minutes, drain, and blend to a paste. Ma'amoul keep in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 weeks.
photoBrief: Pale golden ma'amoul cookies with pressed patterns, lightly dusted with icing sugar, on a ceramic plate, one broken open to show the dark date filling, a wooden mould beside them. Warm light. Square 1:1.

title: CHOCOLATE DATE *truffles*
name: Chocolate date truffles
intro: Fudgy chocolate truffles sweetened only with dates. Ten minutes in a food processor, no baking.
ingredients: 180 g soft Zunera dates, pitted (about 10 Medjool, or Mazafati or Rabia), packed
¼ cup unsweetened cocoa powder, plus extra for rolling
1½ tbsp cashew butter, or any nut butter
½ to ¾ cup almond flour (finely ground Zunera almonds)
steps: Line a small plate with baking paper.
Put the dates, melted coconut oil and water in a food processor and blend until only small bits remain, or a paste forms.
Add the cocoa, vanilla, nut butter and salt, and blend again.
Add the almond flour ¼ cup at a time, blending and scraping down the sides, until the mixture comes together in a sticky ball.
Scoop out 1 tbsp portions and roll them into balls between your palms. Dust your hands with a little cocoa if it sticks.
Roll the truffles in cocoa if you like. Eat them as they are, or freeze for 30 minutes for a firmer truffle. They keep in the fridge for a week, or the freezer for a month.
tip: A food processor works best; a blender struggles with the thick mixture. Shop-bought almond flour works too.
photoBrief: Dark chocolate truffles dusted in cocoa on a small plate, one bitten in half to show the fudgy centre. Dark background, warm light. Square 1:1.

title: DATE & WALNUT *cake*
name: Eggless date & walnut cake
intro: A soft, moist, eggless cake with chopped dates, walnuts and a hint of coffee, made with whole wheat flour.
ingredients: ½ cup finely chopped Zunera Kalmi or Mashrook dates, tightly packed (100 g)
¼ cup finely chopped walnuts (25 g): crack Zunera in-shell walnuts, or use Zunera walnut kernels
1 cup almond milk, or any milk
½ cup raw sugar or regular sugar (110 g)
1 tbsp cacao nibs or small chocolate chips (optional)
¼ cup sunflower oil, or another neutral oil
steps: Finely chop the dates and walnuts. Grease a 7.5 to 8-inch cake pan, or line it with baking paper.
Warm the milk gently in a small pan; do not let it boil. Take it off the heat and stir in the coffee, dates, walnuts and sugar until the sugar and coffee dissolve. Leave to cool for 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, preheat the oven to 200°C for 15 minutes.
Sift the flour, baking powder, baking soda and salt into a mixing bowl. Add the date and milk mixture, the cacao nibs if using, then the oil, water and vanilla.
Whisk or fold just until the batter is even. Do not overmix.
Pour into the pan, scrape in the rest from the bowl, and tap the pan on the counter to level it.
Bake at 190°C for 35 to 40 minutes, until a skewer pushed into the centre and near the edges comes out clean.
Cool on a rack, then slice. Keep leftovers in an airtight box in the fridge for about a week.
tip: Every oven runs differently, so start checking at 35 minutes. All-purpose flour, or half whole wheat and half all-purpose, works in place of whole wheat flour.
photoBrief: A round date and walnut cake on a wooden board, two slices cut to show the crumb, walnut halves beside it and a cup of chai. Warm light. Square 1:1.

title: TOMATO KHEJUR *chutney*
name: Bengali tomato khejur chutney
intro: The sweet, spiced tomato and date chutney served at the end of a Bengali meal, flavoured with panch phoron.
ingredients: 2 dry red chillies, broken and seeds removed
1 inch ginger, finely chopped (or 1 tsp grated)
4 Zunera Fard or Rabbi dates, pitted and chopped (about 2 tbsp)
steps: Heat the mustard oil in a heavy pan on low heat until hot.
Add the panch phoron and red chillies and fry for a few seconds, until they crackle and smell fragrant.
Add the ginger and sauté for a few seconds, until it no longer smells raw. Do not let it brown.
Add the tomatoes and salt and mix well. Cover and cook on low to medium-low heat for 9 to 10 minutes, until the tomatoes are soft and mushy.
Add the raisins, dates, sugar and amchur. Cook for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring often and mashing the tomatoes, until the chutney thickens. Add a splash of water if it starts to stick.
Serve warm or at room temperature. Leftovers keep for 4 to 5 days in the fridge.
tip: How much sugar you need depends on how tart your tomatoes are. Start with 1 tbsp and taste.
photoBrief: A small ceramic bowl of glossy red tomato chutney studded with dates and raisins, on a banana leaf beside rice. Warm light. Square 1:1.

title: SPICED ORANGE & DATE *salad*
name: Spiced orange & date salad
intro: A classic Moroccan pairing: juicy orange, chopped dates, toasted almonds and a dusting of cinnamon. Ready in 15 minutes.
ingredients: ½ cup Zunera Deglet Nour dates, pitted and chopped
¼ cup Zunera almonds, toasted and chopped
steps: Juice one of the oranges.
Peel the other four oranges and cut them into chunks.
In a large bowl, mix the orange juice, orange chunks, dates, almonds and cinnamon until everything is well combined.
Serve as a light dish on its own, or spooned over morning yoghurt.
tip: The original recipe uses Medjool dates. Deglet Nour are firmer and chop neatly, but either works.
photoBrief: A bowl of orange chunks with chopped golden dates and toasted almonds, dusted with cinnamon. Bright daylight. Square 1:1.

title: FIG & WALNUT OVERNIGHT *oats*
name: Fig & walnut overnight oats
intro: Five minutes the night before, and breakfast is waiting in the fridge. Cinnamon oats topped with figs, apple, walnuts and honey.
ingredients: ⅔ cup almond milk, or any milk
¼ cup Zunera dried figs, chopped
steps: Divide the oats, chia seeds and cinnamon between two jars.
Stir the milk and vanilla together and pour half into each jar. Stir well, close the lids, and refrigerate overnight, or for at least 4 hours.
In the morning, top each jar with the apple, figs and walnuts, and drizzle over the honey.
tip: The oats keep in the fridge for up to 4 days. For warm oats, microwave for 30 to 40 seconds before adding the toppings. Use maple syrup instead of honey to make it vegan.
photoBrief: Two glass jars of overnight oats topped with chopped figs, diced apple, walnuts and a drizzle of honey, a spoon resting on one. Morning light. Square 1:1.

title: HOMEMADE DATE *paste*
name: Homemade date paste
intro: One ingredient, one blender. A jar of date paste is the easiest swap for sugar in baking, oats, smoothies and chai.
ingredients: 450 g Zunera dates, pitted (any variety: Khudri, Fard, Rabbi, Sufri or Deglet Nour all work)
Hot water, for soaking and blending (optional)
steps: Take out the seeds, if your dates have them: cut or pull each date open and lift the seed out.
If the dates are on the dry side, or your blender is not very strong, soak them in hot water for 30 minutes to soften, then drain.
Blend the dates until smooth and paste-like. This can take a while, so rest the machine every few minutes so it does not overheat.
If it will not come together, add hot water one tablespoon at a time.
When it is smooth and lump-free, spoon it into a clean, airtight jar.
tip: Firmer dates such as Khudri, Fard, Rabbi and Sufri benefit from the 30-minute soak. Made without water, the paste keeps in the fridge for 3 to 4 months; with water, up to 1 month. You can also freeze it in an ice-cube tray.
photoBrief: A glass jar of smooth, glossy date paste with a spoon in it, a few whole dates beside it on a linen cloth. Soft natural light. Square 1:1.
